title: Automotive apprentice starter toolkit
summary: Build the starter kit in stages.
body: Begin with the current school or employer list, then mark the tools already owned and any equipment the shop supplies. Buy core drivers, pliers and sockets before optional power or premium diagnostic upgrades.
caution: Check SAE coverage, exact spark-plug sizes, the required feeler-gauge range, hammers, precision rules and fender protection separately. This directory is not a complete school compliance list.

title: Vehicle diagnostics buying plan
summary: Define the required diagnostic function first.
body: Record the vehicle and symptom, confirm the required system access, then check exact tool coverage before ordering. Read codes and live data in the context of service information; clear codes only when the diagnostic procedure calls for it.
caution: Enhanced system access and bidirectional functions vary by vehicle. Include updates, gateway access, adapters and training in the purchase decision.

title: Battery and no-start electrical diagnosis
summary: Separate battery condition from the circuit fault.
body: Inspect the supported low-voltage battery and connections, assess battery/starting/charging behaviour with appropriate equipment, and use a meter when the fault requires circuit measurements. Choose charging or starting support for its intended role.
caution: This is an equipment plan for documented conventional low-voltage applications, not instructions for EV high-voltage work. Match chemistry and ratings to every connected device.

title: Wheel removal and refitting equipment plan
summary: Plan support, removal and final tightening together.
body: Check approved lifting points and surface conditions, select suitable lifting and support equipment, then match sockets and access tools to the fasteners. Include an appropriate calibrated torque wrench for the vehicle’s final tightening specification.
caution: A floor jack is not working support. An impact setting does not establish final wheel torque. Check pressure against the vehicle cold-pressure specification after the relevant service checks.

title: Brake service toolkit
summary: Identify the brake design before choosing retraction tools.
body: Start with the vehicle service procedure and inspect the actual brake arrangement. Measuring pads, retracting pistons and bleeding hydraulics require different tools; buy only the supported method and adapters.
caution: Some rear and EPB systems require a different retraction procedure, while ABS bleeding can require supported scan-tool functions. Do not treat a generic piston compressor or pressure bleeder as universal.

title: Routine servicing and oil-change toolkit
summary: Match access, filter geometry and fluid handling.
body: Confirm the engine’s filter and drain arrangement, plan safe access and capture capacity, and select the correct removal or cap tool. Keep the clean filling container separate from used-fluid capture.
caution: Use the specified fluid, quantity, installation method and tightening requirements. The equipment list does not replace the vehicle procedure, temperature precautions or suitable disposal.

title: Suspension and steering service equipment
summary: Choose separators, pressing equipment and support for the actual assembly.
body: Begin with the vehicle service information and identify whether the operation is separating a tapered stud, pressing a joint, servicing a hub or gaining control-arm access. Check the required adapters and frame clearance before choosing a kit. The OTC 6295 set includes the 6297 separator; they are a set-versus-standalone decision. Use the 7249 for supported pressing arrangements and consult the 6575 application guide for hub work. Include appropriate vehicle support, hand tools and final torque equipment in the plan, and retain suitable workshop equipment already available. A powerful impact wrench is an optional removal aid where the tool instructions permit it, not a substitute for a compatible receiver or a specified tightening procedure.
caution: This is an equipment buying plan, not coil-spring or strut-disassembly instruction. Stored suspension forces, loaded joints and vehicle support require the proper vehicle procedure and competence. Do not apply impact loading to a tool unless its own instructions allow it. Check Hub Grappler coverage beyond its published guide years.

title: Cooling-system diagnosis and refill toolkit
summary: Plan pressure checks, containment, filling and any specific flushing operation.
body: Separate diagnosis from replacing coolant. For pressure checks, choose between a suitable adapter-based tester and a verified universal-fit connection. For refilling, decide whether the vehicle procedure calls for a funnel-based bleeding arrangement or supports a vacuum-assisted refill tool. MV4533 requires shop air; the MV4560 pressure tester uses a hand pump. The updated 24980 funnel kit adds a specific Toyota/Lexus V35A connection but still needs an exact fit check. A backflush tool is only relevant when that separate service operation is appropriate. Add inspection lighting and adequate collection containers, and keep incompatible transmission-fill equipment out of the cooling-system plan.
caution: Follow cool-system temperature and pressure requirements and capture coolant appropriately. Do not treat an 8.8-litre extractor or shallow drip pan as automatic proof of adequate drain capacity. Confirm fluid compatibility and adapter sealing. Vacuum refill and vacuum-hold observations do not establish that every cooling-system fault has been diagnosed.

title: Engine mechanical diagnosis and service toolkit
summary: Match the diagnostic question to the gauge, then keep repair tools in a separate role.
body: Start with the fault evidence and engine service information. A compression tester compares suitable gasoline-engine cylinders under the required test conditions. A leak-down tester instead uses regulated air and correct engine positioning to help investigate leakage paths. Vacuum and low-pressure gauges answer other questions, while a fuel-pressure kit must match the connection and specified pressure range. Code readers, electrical instruments and inspection cameras can provide supporting evidence. The Lisle 51450 is included only as an optional mechanical repair tool when an appropriate harmonic-damper operation follows diagnosis; it does not perform an engine test. Select the relevant equipment rather than treating all these methods as interchangeable.
caution: These gasoline and low-pressure instruments do not establish compatibility with diesel common rail or high-pressure direct injection. Leak-down testing can turn an engine if the setup is wrong; use the vehicle and tester procedures. Match spark-plug thread adapters, ignition/fuel disabling requirements and expected values to the engine. The presence of a code or one abnormal reading does not by itself identify a failed component.

title: Workshop and mobile-mechanic setup
summary: Build around the workspace and the tools already available.
body: Plan lighting, storage, power, compressed air and suitable working surfaces together. A mobile kit needs secure transport and a realistic carrying weight; a workshop may already supply much of the shared equipment.
caution: Choose optional upgrades for recurring work rather than collecting every listed product. Keep hazardous tasks, PPE and lifting/support requirements specific to the workspace and vehicles.
